projects.name: Theatre concept
projects.summary: A performing arts concept inspired by the traditional Omani Gim instrument.
projects.description:
GIM Theater is a cultural and performing arts concept developed for Dhofar Municipality, with a stated project area of 10,000 m². The design takes inspiration from the Gim, a traditional Omani musical instrument made from a conch shell, translating this cultural reference into a sculptural building with flowing curves and overlapping shell-like forms. White exterior surfaces, patterned openings, sweeping glazed façades, and integrated lighting establish a distinctive architectural identity rooted in Oman’s musical heritage.

The concept includes an auditorium with a performance stage, tiered audience seating, and curved balcony levels. Sculpted interior surfaces and layered lighting extend the flowing architectural language into the performance space. Glazed public areas connect visually with the surrounding plazas, while landscaped spaces, pedestrian approaches, and reflecting pools shape the arrival experience and provide places for gathering before and after events. Our scope comprised concept design, establishing the architectural vision, overall building form, and spatial relationships between the performance venue, public areas, and external setting.

Stone-faced walls, coordinated paving, palm planting and low-level lighting establish a consistent character, while perimeter railings define the edges of the viewing areas. Dedicated parking and low-rise visitor facilities support arrival and movement through the destination.

Our full design scope develops these elements as a coordinated visitor environment, with attention to circulation, resting points, coastal views and the relationship between built features and the rocky setting. The design integrates landscape treatment, shade structures, external lighting and visitor facilities to support daytime and evening use. Particular attention is given to the detailing of level transitions, viewing edges and public spaces, creating a coherent sequence from the arrival area to the principal coastal viewpoints.

projects.name: Shoreline protection study
projects.summary: Survey-led coastal engineering and the design of shoreline protection measures.
projects.description:
A coastal engineering project for the Environment Authority addressing shoreline erosion along selected coastal stretches in Oman. The project focuses on developing protection measures suited to the conditions of each study area, with attention to the shoreline, adjacent land uses and the coastal setting. A survey-led approach combines regional coastal mapping, defined study extents and site investigations to establish the geographical context of the works. Drone-based surveying and GNSS positioning support the collection of site information, providing a basis for understanding coastal conditions and informing the development of shoreline protection proposals.

Our scope comprises full design of the coastal protection works. Our approach brings together site survey information, assessment of erosion conditions and evaluation of suitable protection options to develop a coordinated engineering response. The design process considers the relationship between individual intervention areas and the surrounding shoreline, with attention to constructability, maintenance requirements and environmental considerations. As the project progresses, the design is developed around the available site evidence and the Environment Authority’s requirements, providing the basis for the proposed protection works and their detailed documentation.

projects.name: Fisheries industrial masterplan
projects.summary: An integrated fisheries industrial and logistics platform with harbour and marine facilities.
projects.description:
The fisheries sector is one of the principal non-oil pillars of the national economy and a priority area under Oman Vision 2040, supported by an extensive coastline, productive fishing grounds and a strategic position on established export routes. Consistent with this direction, the Ministry is moving the sector beyond primary landing and first-sale activity towards an integrated industrial model, in which fishing, processing, cold chain, aquaculture support, logistics and export services are consolidated within a single planned and serviced location.

The Fishery Industrial City in Qurun has been conceived in response to this direction. It is intended to operate as an integrated industrial and logistics platform serving the fishing fleet, the processing industries and aquaculture production, and to attract private capital through a public–private partnership delivery model.

The total planned area, including the extension, is approximately 6.4 square kilometres.

Located in Sahnout, the development comprises 558 residential units, including detached villas, twin villas, townhouses and apartments, supported by approximately 40,000 square meters of landscaped green space and a comprehensive range of community facilities.

We have served as the multidisciplinary design consultant, delivering the masterplan, urban design, villa architecture, roads, civil infrastructure, utility networks, landscape design, engineering coordination and statutory approvals. The project establishes an integrated framework in which housing, mobility, infrastructure, public spaces and community amenities are planned as one coherent and implementable neighborhood.

The development covers a total area of 450,000 square metres.
